record.original_question: For nonlinear elastostatics, prove that the elastic energy admits minimizers when the stored-energy function W is quasiconvex and satisfies the singular determinant condition W(A) tends to infinity as det A tends to 0 from above, with W(A) infinite when det A is nonpositive so that orientation collapse is excluded.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Prove the existence of energy minimizers for elastostatics for quasiconvex stored-energy functions satisfying (2.7).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic body. A deformation is a map $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$, and its gradient $\nabla u(x)$ takes values in the set $M^{n\times n}$ of real $n\times n$ matrices. Let $M^{n\times n}_+ = \{A \in M^{n\times n} : \det A > 0\}$.

A stored-energy function is a Borel measurable function $W : M^{n\times n} \to [0,\infty]$ satisfying:
(i) (Orientation preservation / non-interpenetration on the energy level) $W(A) = +\infty$ whenever $\det A \le 0$;
(ii) (Singular determinant condition) $W(A) \to +\infty$ as $\det A \to 0^+$, uniformly on bounded subsets of $M^{n\times n}_+$;
(iii) (Quasiconvexity) $W$ is quasiconvex on $M^{n\times n}_+$ in the sense of Morrey: for every $A \in M^{n\times n}_+$ and every $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $A + \nabla\varphi(x) \in M^{n\times n}_+$ a.e.,
$$\int_\Omega W(A + \nabla \varphi(x))\,dx \ge W(A)\,|\Omega|;$$
(iv) (Coercivity) there exist $p \ge 1$ and constants $c > 0$, $b \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $W(A) \ge c|A|^p + b$ for all $A \in M^{n\times n}$.

Consider the energy
$$I(u) = \int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx$$
on an admissible class $\mathcal{A}$ of deformations consisting of maps $u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfying a prescribed Dirichlet boundary condition $u = u_0$ on a portion $\partial\Omega_1 \subset \partial\Omega$ of positive surface measure (with $u_0$ chosen so that $\mathcal{A}$ is nonempty and $\inf_{\mathcal{A}} I < \infty$).

Prove (or disprove) that under hypotheses (i)–(iv) the functional $I$ attains its infimum on $\mathcal{A}$; equivalently, that there exists $u^* \in \mathcal{A}$ with $I(u^*) = \inf_{u \in \mathcal{A}} I(u)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a long-standing open question. It is widely known as Ball's problem of existence of minimizers in nonlinear elastostatics under quasiconvexity together with the singular behavior of $W$ at $\det A = 0^+$. Polyconvex existence theory (Ball, 1977) handles a stronger convexity hypothesis, and partial results exist (e.g., relaxation results, existence with cavitation/fracture, and special cases), but the general quasiconvex case with the singular determinant constraint remains unresolved as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: On the Theory of Relaxation in Nonlinear Elasticity with Constraints on the Determinant
status_evidence.snippet: Variational problems in nonlinear elasticity with energy densities continuous on matrices with positive determinant and diverging to infinity as the determinant tends to zero.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses relaxation under the singular determinant condition, indicating the underlying existence question is not resolved in general.
